'''× ''Fatshedera''''' {{IPAc-en|f|æ|t|s|ˈ|h|ɛ|d|ər|ə}}<ref>''Sunset Western Garden Book,'' 1995:606–607</ref> is  a [[Hybrid (biology)#Hybrid plants|hybrid]] genus of [[flowering plant]]s, [[common name]] '''tree ivy''' or '''aralia ivy'''. It has only one species, '''× ''Fatshedera lizei'''''. The hybrid symbol × in front of the name indicates that this is an inter-generic hybrid, a cross between plants from different [[genus|genera]]. The name may be displayed with or without a space after the × symbol.

× ''Fatshedera lizei'' was created by crossing ''[[Fatsia japonica]]'' 'Moserii' (Moser's Japanese fatsia, the seed parent) and ''[[Hedera helix]]'' (common ivy, the pollen parent) at the Lizé Frères tree nursery at [[Nantes]] in France in 1912. Its generic name is derived from the names of the two parent genera.

==Description==
The plant combines the [[shrub]]by shape of ''[[Fatsia]]'' with the five-lobed leaves of ''[[Hedera]]''. As a shrub, × ''F. lizei'' can grow up to {{Convert abbreviated|1.2|m|ft}} tall, above which the weight of the fairly weak branches makes them tend to bend over. It can, however, also be tied to a support and grow into a [[vine]] up to {{Convert abbreviated|3-4|m}} tall; unlike ''Hedera'', it does not readily climb without assistance. The [[leaf]] blades are {{Convert abbreviated|7-25|cm}} long and broad, with a {{Convert abbreviated|5-20|cm}} petiole. The [[flower]]s are 4–6 mm in diameter, yellowish-white, produced in late autumn or early winter in dense [[umbel]]s; they are usually [[infertility|sterile]] and do not produce any fruit. However, specimens have been reported which did produce not only flowers but also clusters of berries, one of which put forth shoots in the pot.{{citation needed|date=June 2024}}

==Taxonomy==
It was first described as ''Aralia'' × ''lizei'' {{au|Cochet}} by [[Pierre Charles Marie Cochet]] in 1912. It was later transferred to its own hybrid genus × ''Fatshedera'' {{au|Guillaumin}} as × ''Fatshedera lizei'' {{au|(Cochet) Guillaumin}} by [[André Guillaumin]] in 1923.<ref name="POWO b">{{Cite web |title=× Fatshedera Guillaumin {{!}} Plants of the World Online {{!}} Kew Science |url=http://powo.science.kew.org/taxon/urn:lsid:ipni.org:names:3012-1 |access-date=2025-05-28 |website=Plants of the World Online |language=en}}</ref><ref name = "POWO a" /> It is an artificial hybrid of ''[[Fatsia japonica]]'' and ''[[Hedera hibernica]]''.<ref name = "POWO a" />

==Cultivation==
It is grown both as a garden plant outdoors and as a [[houseplant]] indoors, where its tolerance of shady conditions is valued. Inside, it grows well in bright indirect light. Outdoors, it can tolerate winter temperatures down to {{Convert|-15|C}}, but can also be grown successfully indoors with temperatures never falling below {{Convert|20|C}}. Several [[cultivar]]s have been selected, with dark green to variously white- or yellow-[[variegation|variegated]] leaves.

× ''Fatshedera lizei'',<ref>{{cite web|title=RHS Plant Selector - × ''Fatshedera lizei''|url= https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/51972/x-Fatshedera-lizei/Details | accessdate=1 July 2020}}</ref> together with the [[cultivar]]s 'Annemieke'<ref>{{cite web|title=RHS Plant Selector - × ''Fatshedera lizei'' 'Annemieke'|url= https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/67002/x-Fatshedera-lizei-Annemieke-(v)/Details |accessdate=1 July 2020}}</ref> and 'Variegata'<ref>{{cite web|title=RHS Plant Selector - × ''Fatshedera lizei'' 'Variegata'|url= https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/79636/x-Fatshedera-lizei-Variegata-(v)/Details |accessdate=1 July 2020}}</ref> have gained the [[Royal Horticultural Society]]'s [[Award of Garden Merit]].<ref>{{cite web  | url= https://www.rhs.org.uk/plants/pdfs/agm-lists/agm-ornamentals.pdf | title = AGM Plants - Ornamental | date = July 2017 | page = 38 | publisher = Royal Horticultural Society | accessdate = 26 February 2018}}</ref>
